name: Mythic Storyteller (lamp-lit paper theatre)
summary: A storyteller's performance of a myth: lamp-lit layered paper, public-domain photographs of the tradition's own art cut out and mounted as plates, haloes and gold leaf on sacred figures, jointed puppets for action, ornament that names the tradition. Reverent and handmade; motion behaves like paper placed by hand and a lamp carried from scene to scene, never like software.
avoid_for: debunking or devotional sermons (the stance is storyteller)

identity.mood: reverent, warm, wondrous; tension without gore
identity.visual_language: layered deckle-edged paper, duotoned museum photographs as cut plates, gold leaf, ornament bands, shadow-theatre silhouettes
identity.editorial_approach: the storyteller's frame is visible: name the text and version, then perform the episode as a diorama the lamp moves through
identity.illustration_style: flat mineral colour with a dark contour, after the tradition's own painting (Pattachitra, Kalpasutra, black-figure, picture stones)
identity.photography_style: public-domain museum objects (sculpture, manuscripts, vases, picture stones) duotoned to ink and paper, mounted with a paper margin or cut to silhouette
identity.composition_philosophy: one sacred or heroic figure dominant and high in the frame, 2-4 paper planes of world behind, ornament at the edge; deities never at foot level
identity.environment: a paper diorama under a warm lamp: hills, peaks, waves, clouds and gateways as cut sheets
identity.realism: flat and handmade; photographs are objects in the diorama, not windows
identity.storytelling_conventions: invocation and source first; acts change by light and palette; the gods' approval by gold and falling flowers; the closing returns to the opening lamp

colors.evidence: Rag-paper ground; Pattachitra conch-shell white (research-visual-design, Pattachitra)
Gold leaf (Tanjore, Kalpasutra); shapes and display only
Malachite; Kerala mural green for serene figures

palette.contrast_strategy: dark ink on warm paper for all text (13.9:1); vermilion and lapis pass AA for large text; gold is never text.

typography.display: Playfair Display 700 (carved-relief: EB Garamond in spaced capitals)
typography.mono: IBM Plex Mono only for source and accession lines
typography.scale_and_hierarchy: one invocation title per film; cartouche names the source; labels name the figure and its emblem

composition.principles: sacred figure centred or on the upper third, framed by an arch, halo or niche; 3+ overlapping paper planes; ornament band at the edge in folio scenes
composition.negative_space: paper fibre and lamp falloff fill quiet areas; never a flat empty field
composition.layering_and_depth: 4-6 planes with soft lifted shadows and parallax at 2-3 speeds

design_system.shape_language: deckled hills, peaks, waves, clouds, flames and lotus petals; arches and niches for the sacred
design_system.texture: rag-paper fibre, deckle edges, duotone grain on photographs, gold-leaf glint
design_system.materials: paper, gold leaf, dyed leather, stone and terracotta (as photographs)
design_system.lighting: one warm lamp, flickering slowly; vignette at the edges; the lamp can travel to the scene that matters
design_system.visual_rhythm: establish the world wide, hold the sacred figure close, return wide at the close
design_system.image_treatment: duotone to ink and paper so plates from different museums sit together; sticker edge for cut-outs; never a raw stock photograph

motion.grammar: Paper is placed by hand and lifted away; sacred figures rise slowly and are held with breathing and a turning halo; puppets move from their joints; the lamp breathes all the time.

easing.entrances: enter-decel for paper (power3.out); a slow rise for sacred figures (power2.out, 1.4-1.8 s); no overshoot on any deity
easing.exits: exit-accelerate (lift away) or a dissolve under the lamp
easing.emphasis: gold glint or a halo swell, not a bounce

timing.pace: measured; a visual event every 2-3 s, slower holds on the sacred figure with breathing under them
timing.holds: allowed on the sacred image with breathe, halo turn and lamp flicker under it

vocabulary: kaavad doors opening onto the next panel
scroll unroll / lamp carried to the next scene
paper lifted away, revealing the sheet beneath
avoid: shattering, exploding or wiping a deity image
spin and zoom-through on sacred figures
transitions.continuity: the lamp, the halo or an ornament band carries the eye across the cut

camera.language: a slow push into the diorama and gentle parallax; the camera bows to the sacred figure (push in and hold), never orbits it

motion.object_movement: paper planes sway slightly; waves and clouds drift; puppets gesture from pivots
motion.kinetic_typography: invocation title word by word; source cartouche; figure labels with their emblem
motion.particles: flower shower for divine approval, embers for fire and sacrifice, sparingly
motion.stillness_policy: A held sacred image always has breathing, a turning halo and the lamp flicker under it; no frozen frame under narration.

audio_direction.narration: warm storyteller (af_bella or bm_george), 1.0-1.1x, unhurried; names the source and version once
audio_direction.music: a dim drone and one tradition-appropriate timbre (tanpura and bansuri, lyre, tagelharpa) at -24 to -28 LUFS; never a pastiche of a sacred chant
audio_direction.sfx: paper rustle, a lamp wick, temple bell or conch only where the story has one, 12-18 dB under the voice
audio_direction.silence_and_space: a breath before the sacred figure appears and after the teaching line

rendering.strategy: Programmatic SVG/CSS paper diorama in HyperFrames through the mythic kit (Studio.kit.mythic), with public-domain museum photographs (scripts/myth-sources.py) imported as plates and AI-generated stills only where no public-domain image exists, each one iconography-checked.
rendering.resource_notes: SVG filters (fibre, soft shadow, glow) are the heaviest part; keep photo plates under about 1600 px on the long side.

provenance.method: Authored rule set (prescribed) from web research on 2026-11-23: Reiniger and Ocelot silhouette films, Sita Sings the Blues, Cartoon Saloon, kamishibai and toy theatre, Pattachitra, Phad, kaavad, Tholu Bommalata, Kerala murals, Tanjore, Kalpasutra, Ajanta, Greek vase painting, Karagiozis, Gotland picture stones. Sources: .claude/skills/mythic-tales/references/design-language.md.
provenance.notes: Every value is prescribed intent, not a measurement; several pigment notes rest on blog sources and all hex values are estimates from pigment names. Evidence of use goes under validation after a render.

weaknesses: Generated figures hallucinate iconography (wrong number of arms, wrong emblem); every one needs the tradition pack's checklist.
Duotone can flatten a museum photograph's detail; check legibility of the subject at phone size.
Paper shadows read as cheap if their direction is inconsistent across planes.
Placeholder puppet figures look generic; a real film needs traced or commissioned silhouettes.
example_scenes: Invocation: lamp flickers on rag paper, a lotus border draws, 'As told in the Valmiki Ramayana' slides in.
Revelation: a duotoned museum relief of the deity rises inside a niche plate while a prabhavali blooms behind it and gold glints.
Turn: kaavad doors open onto the inner panel; the palette swaps to vermilion and ink for the threat, then back as blossoms fall.
